## My theory of change (why I do this work)

1.  I try to discover true facts that will be useful and interesting
    - Animal advocacy has an [evidence problem](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/svjqgyFuFQ34qSgmw/animal-welfare-has-an-evidence-problem) across many domains
    - Donors build these big complicated CEA models on weak foundations; I want to improve those foundations
2.  A lot of papers are like 'this one weird trick will solve [pressing social problem]' and I live to fight them
    - The point of <https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/> is basically "you should not take (some piece of) research at face value because [publication bias/misleading presentation/mismatch between strength of evidence & strength of claim/etc.]"
3.  If the advocates do their own evaluations they'll all say how great they are

## My *lab's* theory of change {.t}

I actually had to think about this for a fundraising thing (inputs, outputs, outcomes, and impact):

\centering

\includegraphics[width=\linewidth, height=0.7\textheight, keepaspectratio]{images/TOC.png}

## My take: if you don't articulate your TOC and design your research around it, you might default to a TOC that makes no sense

1.  'Effect change within my field'
    - This is fine if you can pull it off but it's A LOT OF WORK. Talk to Kristof/Kevin Kuruc/Bob Fischer about this
2.  Join the vegan echo chamber
    - Write papers like 'carnists score higher on sociopathy/RWA measures' or 'it is ethically justified to serve your colleagues a vegan meal'
3.  'My thing definitely works and everyone should invest in it'
    - Once you *know* the answer to the big questions, it's really hard to do research because [you're no longer searching](https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/p/the-problem-with-politicized-research)
    - Aesthetic objection: this profanes our sacred duty to seek truth
    - Just go get an advocacy job instead

::: notes
- That's not to say a theory of change doesn't exist just because I don't understand it.
- Drunk searching for his keys where the light is. It's the hammer you have; it doesn't necessarily make sense for the problem of veganism.
- Philosophy in particular: hard to imagine one more philosophy paper, especially in the language of academic philosophy rather than plain language, meaningfully changing anyone's consumption. If it did, we would see evidence of it in studies. Maybe philosophers need to do that kind of work so other people can make sense of it.
- Or you can try to show that veganism is an interesting case of something else, but again, not so sure.
:::

## So what's your TOC?

- The fact that I don't understand what you do is neither here nor there (who cares what I think)
- If you want someone to take your work and run with it, what does that look like?
  - Who would it be?
- If you think your question is interesting, what is it a case of?
  - What broader phenomenon are you hoping to illuminate?
- Thanks!
